```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
has_ggplot <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```

studysynth makes fake participants for a REDCap study, so you can write and test analysis code before anyone real has enrolled. It reads your project's *structure* and a YAML spec saying how your measures behave. It never reads real subject data.

## A fake study

The package ships with Calm Minds, an invented mindfulness trial for depression: PHQ-9 screening, baseline, a two-week experience sampling burst, and three follow-ups.

```{r}
library(studysynth)

spec <- example_path("calm_minds.yaml")
check_spec(spec)
```

The checker compares every field, form, and event in the spec against the REDCap project, and makes sure the models parse and a few people can be synthesized.

```{r}
fake <- synthesize(spec, n = 60, seed = 1)
study_flow(fake)
```

The result is in REDCap import format, one row per person per event (and per prompt for experience sampling):

```{r}
fake[1:5, 1:8]
```

## Look at it

Scale scores by event and group, with individual people faintly behind:

```{r, eval = has_ggplot}
plot_trajectories(fake, "phq9")
```

Baseline PHQ-9 scores drop at week 4 in *both* groups. People were screened in for being high, so they regress toward the mean, as they do in real trials.

The latent values behind the responses are kept, so you can check whether your analysis recovers what went in:

```{r}
head(true_scores(fake))
```

## Score it

`score_scales()` sums each scale or subscale, reversing items with negative loadings:

```{r}
scored <- score_scales(fake)
summary(scored$phq9_score)
```

`write_scorify_scoresheet()` writes a [scorify](https://github.com/njvack/scorify) scoresheet that scores the same way, for use on your real export.

## Your own study

```{r, eval = FALSE}
use_studysynth("my-fake-study", xml = "MyStudy_metadata.xml")
```

This makes a folder with your REDCap file, a draft `spec.yaml`, a `sources/` folder for your scales' papers, and a `CLAUDE.md` telling a language model how to fill in the spec from those papers. Then tune the spec in the editor with `edit_spec("my-fake-study/spec.yaml")`, and `synthesize()` when it looks right.

See `example_path("calm_minds.yaml")` for a commented example of every spec block.
